subject: Post-call: inference budgeting & ROI playbook for Econopay
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lucia Alvarez <lucia.alvarez@econopay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: inference budgeting & ROI playbook for Econopay

Hi Lucia — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and tangible next steps so we’re aligned on budget framing and technical levers we discussed. I’ve kept this tight for your finance and engineering stakeholders.

What we heard (pain points)
- High per-transaction inference cost when running enrichments for authorization flows (peak QPS spikes).
- Current SLA target of <120ms tail is non-negotiable for checkout flows.
- Budget: initial pilot cap ~ $6k/mo; long-term run-rate needs clear path to <$25k/mo for 10M monthly transactions.

Goals you stated
- Validate that Redwood can meet the <120ms 99th percentile with a realistic pilot volume (100k - 500k tx/month).
- Demonstrate token-econ where per-transaction incremental cost < $0.003 using batching + KV caching.
- Produce an ROI case for finance that shows payback within 3–6 months from conversion uplift and fraud reduction.

Cost levers we recommend (high level)
- Dynamic batching: group small auth lookups into micro-batches during spikes (saves ~30–50% on per-token compute for similar accuracy profiles).
- Prefix/KV caching: cache stability/context for returning sessions — cuts repeated token decode and reduces long-context overhead.
- Quantization profile: 8-bit/INT8 for low-latency decoder paths on your dedicated pool (slight perf tradeoff but big cost wins).
- Route by SLA: serve critical checkout traffic to dedicated low-latency pool; non-critical enrichment to lower-cost variants.

Pilot proposal & metrics
- Duration: 8 weeks (2 weeks ramp, 4 weeks steady, 2 weeks validation).
- Pilot capacity: reserved pool sized for 200 qps peak; burst to shared pool allowed under budget cap.
- Metrics: 99p latency (target <120ms), cost per enriched transaction (target <$0.003), percent served from cache (goal 40%+), model-quality delta (A/B to baseline).

Attachments: I’ve attached a simple token-modeling workbook and a short batching options brief for your engineering and finance teams to review.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Lucia: share a sample daily transaction profile and a representative payload (anonymized) so we can run realistic token modeling (due: Wed, 10 Oct).
2) Econopay finance: confirm pilot budget owner and PO cadence (cc’d finance) — if $6k/mo pilot needs PO, we can queue a billing exception.
3) Marissa/Karthik (internal): I’ll prepare a detailed pilot SOW and a cost sensitivity slide for next Tuesday’s internal pricing review.

If you prefer, we can do a short 20-min follow-up with your finance + infra folks to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: econopay_token-modeling-v1.xlsx (xlsx))
(Attachment: redwood-batching-options.pdf (pdf))

- We’ll anonymize and send a 7-day transaction sample by tomorrow EOD. It’ll include avg payload size, peak minutes, and known spike patterns.
- Pilot budget: I can own the $6k for the pilot but will need a short PO for accounting — I’ll route that this week.
- For the SLA routing: can you confirm how automatic fallback works if the dedicated pool hits capacity? We need guaranteed continuity during black-Friday-like spikes.

Agree a 20-min walkthrough is useful; I’ll pull in head of infra (cc’d finance for PO visibility). Suggested times: Mon 11 Oct 10:00–10:30am PT or Tue 12 Oct 2:30–3:00pm PT.

Lucia
